questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Please explain: *
questions.answer: I went in exchange to get a break from my everyday life. I wanted to study somewhere else, and by that put som perspective on my life back home.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a big, well known city. I was in Prague and I had heard a lot of good stuff about the city and had been there myself one time. I also read that the University was well recognized. The expenses of the destination also played a role, where Prague was fairly cheap.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. We got some emails with the information about our study program and so on. Not complicated. Although something you need to be aware of. They say that the semester ends at a certain date, but in my case, my exams were way earlier. You get your exam dates, when you begin the University at your destination.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. We found it on a website. Also easy to find on facebook if you are a part of the erasmus housing groups in Prague. We used a website called Prague Shared Flats. There you can contact the landlord. He is a bit weird, but everything was alright, and worked out in the end.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive, but you can live in the citycenter with other nice students, if you find a student apartment. It provides a homely feel.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. Only had to get a student card and register my chosen courses online.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Its pretty easy-going. Just follow the steps they provide you on email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everyone. Although some had limited capacity, but you just have to be ready and fast at the specific time they are enrolled on the website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All of the education in my courses was solely lectures, so that was a bit boring. The teachers can be pretty hard to understand sometimes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were pretty easy. Very straightforward. Had some knowledge in advance as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In UCPH you know the teacher way more and its easier and more accessible to ask for help. In my courses it was only the teacher who spoke, while you participate way more in UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on some trips to some of the cities in the neighboring countries, like Vienna, Budapest or Bratislava. Go on some hikes in Czechia. Go watch icehockey thats fun. Just walk a lot around in the different neighborhoods. Go to dogs bar :). Good viewpoint in letna park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: All the things you find overwhelming or unmanageable before you leave, with all the things you need to find out, will be well worth it. Its not that complicated as it seems. Try to socialize as much as possible in the beginning and attend som student events and be open-minded. That makes the overall stay a lot easier. Everybody is just as nervous as you.
